title: Stranglethorn Vale
body: Stranglethorn Vale is a vast, sweltering jungle at the southern end of the Eastern Kingdoms, running from the borders of Duskwood down to a rugged cape on the Great Sea. It was once the heart of the Gurubashi Empire, and the ruins of troll cities lie everywhere beneath the vines. The old capital, Zul'Gurub, still broods in the northeast, where the blood god Hakkar has been called back into the world. What remains of the Gurubashi has splintered into warring tribes, chief among them the Bloodscalps of the north and the Skullsplitters of the eastern hills. Outsiders have come for the jungle's riches and dangers alike: big game hunters, Venture Company miners and loggers, a Stormwind expedition gone bad under Colonel Kurzen, and the ogres of the Mosh'Ogg mound. The Horde holds Grom'gol on the western shore. On the southern cape the goblin port of Booty Bay trades with all comers, while Bloodsail pirates prowl its waters and Stranglethorn Fever lurks in the undergrowth.

title: Rebel Camp
body: Northwest of the road that enters the jungle from Duskwood, a handful of soldiers hold a small camp under Lieutenant Doren. They once marched under Colonel Kurzen and served him with fierce loyalty, until his descent into corruption twisted that loyalty into rage and they broke away. Outnumbered by their former comrades, they live by guile. Sergeant Yohwa plans raids on the compound to the east, Brother Nimetz searches troll legends for the cause of Kurzen's fall, and supplies, land mines among them, come up from Booty Bay. Even here they are not safe: a traitor within the camp once passed their secrets to the enemy.

title: Nesingwary's Expedition
body: Beside a freshwater river inlet in northern Stranglethorn, near old docks left by some forgotten people, the dwarf Hemet Nesingwary pitched the base camp from which he hunted the Vale. His son, Hemet Nesingwary Jr., now keeps the camp while the elder pursues bigger prey in more exotic lands. Ajeck Rouack teaches the hunting of tigers, Sir S. J. Erlgadin the tracking of panthers, and the faithful Barnil Stonepot keeps the camp in order. Strangers are not readily welcomed. Those who prove themselves against the beasts of the jungle may join the hunt, and each test brings a fiercer quarry.

title: Kurzen's Compound
body: East of the Rebel Camp stands the fortified compound of Colonel Kurzen's expedition, whose jungle fighters outnumber the rebels ten to one. Medicine men tend their wounded with jungle remedies and poison their foes with venom fern extract, and wranglers keep tigers and panthers trained as beasts of war. The camp's logistics officer, Bookie Herod, kept his office on the top floor of its only two-story house. Behind it all a cavern called the Stockpile runs into the hills, where Kurzen's most highly trained men gather and the colonel commands from deep within.

title: Venture Co. Base Camp
body: Near Lake Nazferiti, the goblins of the Venture Company have cut a logging and mining camp out of the jungle. Lumberjacks and shredders fell the trees while geologists hunt the strange blue crystals found in the hills, which the company tumbles and treats, apparently for use as a fuel or catalyst. Foreman Cozzle runs the work from a house at the operations center, where he keeps the blueprints for a new fuel regulator fitted to his shredders under lock and key. The company's greed has made it enemies, not least among the goblins of Booty Bay, who complain it leaves no room for honest trade.

title: Bal'lal Ruins
body: The Bal'lal Ruins and the nearby Tkashi Ruins are crumbling Gurubashi sites in the north of the Vale, held by warriors, axe throwers and shamans of the Bloodscalp tribe. Among the stones of Bal'lal lies an ancient tablet carved with a troll legend called Moon Over the Vale, one of four tablets Brother Nimetz hoped would explain Kurzen's madness. The Farstriders of Quel'Thalas have taken an interest too. One of their rangers noticed that the Bloodscalps here fight much like the Amani of the northern forests, and traced their unusual magic to an unexpected patron: a water elemental named Naias.

title: Ruins of Zul'Kunda
body: Zul'Kunda is a sprawling troll ruin near the northern coast and the seat of the Bloodscalp tribe. Their chief, Gan'zulah, and his witch doctor, Nezzliok the Dire, rule from deep within, while headhunters stalk Zul'Kunda and the neighboring Zuuldaia Ruins carrying the shrunken heads of their victims. The Bloodscalps are sworn enemies of the Darkspear and wage war on the Skullsplitter tribe. Two ancient tablets stand among the ruins, one telling of the Fall of Gurubashi and the other of the Emperor's Tomb, relics of the empire that raised these walls.

title: The Vile Reef
body: Off the Savage Coast lie the drowned ruins of an old troll city, sunk beneath the waves when a great shudder of the earth struck long ago. The Darkspear call the place the Vile Reef, for Saltscale murlocs now dwell among its broken stones and attack any who draw near, while giant clams cling to the walls. A tablet in the ruins tells the tale of Gri'lek, a hero of troll legend whose story is sacred to the Darkspear. The reef also hides the Altar of the Tides, a sunken shrine bound up with the cursed Stone of the Tides.

title: Grom'gol Base Camp
body: Grom'gol is the Horde's walled stronghold on the western coast of Stranglethorn. Commander Aggro'gosh holds it for the Warchief, and its first duty is to keep a chain of supply open to Stonard in the Swamp of Sorrows. The Horde did not come to make war on the jungle, but raptors prowl outside the walls and Mosh'Ogg ogres squatting in the nearby Mizjah Ruins ambush its caravans. Zeppelins link the camp to Orgrimmar and the Undercity. Darkspear trolls such as Nimboya and the witch doctor Kin'weelay serve here too, back in the jungle their tribe once called home, though the local tribes count the Darkspear as enemies.

title: Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound
body: In the eastern mountains of Stranglethorn, not far from Zul'Gurub, the Mosh'Ogg ogres have made their home in a great mound with a cave at its heart. Warmongers, maulers and spellcrafters guard its slopes, and deep inside dwells the ogre mage Mai'Zoth, keeper of a jewel called the Mind's Eye. The clan's reach spreads beyond the mound, for Mosh'Ogg brutes also squat in the Mizjah Ruins near Grom'gol. The ogres will even gamble with outsiders: a Booty Bay gambler named Maury once won so much from them that he was chased off the mound.

title: Ruins of Zul'Mamwe
body: Zul'Mamwe lies in a mountain-ringed valley in the east of the Vale, south of the Mosh'Ogg mound. It is the stronghold of the Skullsplitters, the second great troll tribe of Stranglethorn and bitter rivals of the Bloodscalps. Their chief, Ana'thek the Cruel, holds the ruins with the clan witch doctor Mogh the Undying, whose kind carry the fetishes of the tribe's dark magic. The Skullsplitters keep piles of trophy skulls here and at the nearby ruins of Balia'mah and Ziata'jai. Strangely, one of Kurzen's soldiers walks among them too, his mind enslaved by Mogh.

title: Crystalvein Mine
body: Crystalvein Mine is a source of the Singing Crystals, blue stones found only in Stranglethorn and prized by certain buyers. The Venture Company covets the mine but cannot get in, for its tunnels are infested with basilisks, which eat the crystal and draw their hardened hides from it, so the goblins make do with digging in the surrounding hills. Pulsing blue shards cut from the Ironjaw basilisks inside are rare and potent. A Darkspear witch doctor has used them to bend a powerful relic to his will, and says the shards sing to him.

title: Yojamba Isle
body: Off the northwestern coast of the Vale lies Yojamba Isle, where envoys of the Zandalar tribe have made their camp. The Zandalari defeated the blood god Hakkar at Zul'Gurub in ages past, and now that he has risen there again they have returned to Stranglethorn to oppose him, calling on outsiders of every race to help. Servants of King Rastakhan gather here, among them Molthor, the Hand of Rastakhan, and Jin'rokh the Breaker, envoy of the Fist of Rastakhan. They tend the Altar of Zanza and keep a captured Hakkari zealot under guard.

title: Gurubashi Arena
body: North of Booty Bay, in the jungle of the cape, stands a great stone arena raised by the Gurubashi trolls. In ancient days its fights were to the death, and its sand was stained with troll blood. The empire is gone but the bloodletting is not. A pirate called Short John Mithril presides over the sport now. From time to time he leaves a chest of treasure on the arena floor for whoever can claim it, and rivals of every race gather to fight over the prize. Those who triumph again and again are named Grandmaster of the Arena.

title: Mistvale Valley
body: Mistvale Valley is a jungle valley on the Cape of Stranglethorn, home to great troops of gorillas, from the elder Mistvale apes to their silverback patriarchs. In a hidden cave on the southern cape, called the Spirit Den, lives Witch Doctor Unbagwa. He prizes gorilla fangs and claims the power to call up Mokk the Savage, an elusive white beast whose heart is said to be the only cure for Stranglethorn Fever, provided someone guards him from the angry apes while he works.

title: Nek'mani Wellspring
body: High in the cliffs above the Southern Savage Coast, on the western side of the cape, lies a holy spring said to hold the only clean fresh water south of Duskwood. Its sanctity is bitterly disputed: scholars of nearly every race claim its waters were made divine for their own people. Lately an expedition of naga explorers has advanced on the spring and guards it fiercely, and a rarely seen naga, Lord Sakrasis, walks among them. The far seer of Grom'gol counts the water as the final reagent of a powerful enchantment.

title: Ruins of Aboraz
body: Northeast of Booty Bay, the ruins of Aboraz and neighboring Jubuwal have become the domain of Zanzil the Outcast. Feared by his own people for his power over the minds of others, Zanzil feeds a mixture of jungle plants to those who fall into his hands, leaving them strong of body and empty of will. Zombies, naga and troll witch doctors now serve him among the stones. Gamblers who owed money in Booty Bay, once thought to have skipped town, wander here cursed and bewitched, and Yenniku, a captive son of the Darkspear chief, is held here as well.

title: Booty Bay
body: Booty Bay is a goblin port built into the cliffs around Blackwater Cove at the tip of the cape, entered on foot through the bleached jaws of a giant shark. It belongs to the Steamwheedle Cartel and is run by Baron Revilgaz and the Blackwater Raiders, who keep their seat atop the Salty Sailor Tavern. Ships sail from its docks as far as Ratchet. Every race is welcome so long as it brings coin and keeps the peace, and the town's bruisers fall hard on anyone who spills blood on neutral ground. In the jungle camps they whisper that goblins sometimes drag drunken sailors onto slave boats bound for who knows where.

title: Wild Shore
body: The Wild Shore runs along the southern tip of the cape, east of Booty Bay, and the Bloodsail Buccaneers have made it their southern command post. Their camps on the sand teem with deckhands, swashbucklers and warlocks, and their charts and written orders are kept close at hand. Just offshore ride three Bloodsail ships, the Crimson Veil, the Riptide and the Damsel's Luck, and Fleet Master Firallon commands from below decks on the Crimson Veil. From here the pirates plot the fall of Booty Bay. Bottles washed up on these beaches have carried pleas for help from an island farther out to sea.

title: Jaguero Isle
body: Jaguero Isle rises from the South Seas off the cape, a wild island ruled by Skymane gorillas and stalked by jungle cats. Their master is King Mukla, a great Skymane who keeps a prisoner chained there: Princess Poobah, a tauren so far from home that the stars at night seem foreign to her. On clear days she can see the Wild Shore across the water, and she casts notes in bottles into the sea in the hope that someone will find them and come to set her free.

title: Janeiro's Point
body: Janeiro's Point is a rocky island off the coast near Booty Bay, crowned by a towering statue of a goblin with arms spread wide in welcome to ships making for the bay. Its only resident now is Mok'rash, one of three sea giants who wrecked Captain Hecklebury Smotts's ships and killed his crews three times over. The giant bellows across the water day after day, calling for Smotts to come out and fight, and complaining that the statue makes poor company.

title: Hemet Nesingwary Jr.
body: Hemet Nesingwary Jr. is the dwarven son of the famous big game hunter Hemet Nesingwary, a renowned war hero of the Alliance. With his father away chasing bigger prey in more exotic lands, the younger Hemet leads the expedition camp in northern Stranglethorn alongside his father's old companions. Like his father he is slow to welcome strangers, but those who prove themselves against raptors, tigers and panthers may earn a place in the great hunt, and a chance at King Bangalash, the white tiger that brought him to the Vale.

title: Baron Revilgaz
body: Baron Revilgaz rules Booty Bay from his balcony atop the Salty Sailor Tavern, a self-described humble servant of the Steamwheedle Cartel who always wants to know what a visitor can do for him. His Blackwater Raiders keep the port in goblin hands, and he leaves its day-to-day troubles to trusted subordinates such as Krazek and Kebok. Few would dare challenge him, for no one crosses Revilgaz and lives to tell of it. His private passion is the lore of the Gurubashi, and he collects ancient troll relics with real hunger. The Bloodsail Buccaneers want him dead.

title: Fleet Master Seahorn
body: Fleet Master Seahorn is the old sea dog who commands the Blackwater Raiders' fleet of swashbucklers and stands at Baron Revilgaz's side as his most trusted advisor. To him the idea of the Bloodsail Buccaneers storming Booty Bay sounds like madness, and he scorns Fleet Master Firallon as a captain unfit to sail a skiff across a lake. Yet when proof of the plot reaches him he does not wait for the blow to fall. Rather than send his whole fleet, he sends a few skilled fighters to cut down the Bloodsail leadership before they can strike.

title: Fleet Master Firallon
body: Fleet Master Firallon is the human captain of the Bloodsail Buccaneers, the pirate fleet that has Booty Bay in its sights. From below decks on the Crimson Veil he drew up a plan for one great assault: ships closing in from the sea, an artillery barrage to bottle up the harbor, a landing party to put the town to the torch, and the black spot for Revilgaz and Seahorn. His orders even mention salvage for a project with VanCleef in the Deadmines. He welcomes those who make themselves enemies of Booty Bay, and a bold enough ally who strikes down its leaders may be named an admiral of the Bloodsail navy.

title: Colonel Kurzen
body: Colonel Kurzen was once a great and noble man, a soldier of Stormwind who led an expedition into Stranglethorn and whose men followed him with fierce loyalty. Somewhere in the jungle he fell into cruelty and madness, and his soldiers became the instruments of it. Even his enemies concede his brilliance as a tactician: the rebels who broke from him say no menace in these jungles had his cruel intellect. He commands from deep within the Stockpile behind his compound. Brother Nimetz believes the colonel did not fall on his own, but was corrupted by the ogre mage Mai'Zoth.

title: Lieutenant Doren
body: Lieutenant Doren leads the small band of rebels who broke away from Colonel Kurzen. He and his soldiers were once fiercely loyal to the colonel, and watched that devotion twist into rage as Kurzen sank into corruption. Now they hold a camp near the Duskwood road, badly outnumbered. Doren is a careful commander who sends trusted men to spy on the compound and keeps their missions known to only a few, and the betrayal of a soldier he thought brave and true wounds him deeply. He fears the rebels cannot survive alone, and pins his hopes on outsiders willing to carry the fight into the Stockpile.

title: Mai'Zoth
body: Mai'Zoth is an ogre mage who dwells deep within the Mosh'Ogg mound in the eastern mountains of Stranglethorn. He holds the Mind's Eye, a jewel spoken of in Darkspear legend that makes his magic stronger still, and he is said to use it to bend the minds of others to his will. Brother Nimetz of the Rebel Camp is certain it was Mai'Zoth who corrupted Colonel Kurzen. The Darkspear remember him from the days when their tribe still lived in the jungle as vicious and strong in magic, and their greatest witch doctor has sought his jewel to save a lost son of the tribe.

title: Nimboya
body: Nimboya is a Darkspear troll sent from distant Orgrimmar back to Stranglethorn on a grim errand. As was his people's custom, his chief's youngest son, Yenniku, was given to the Gurubashi of Zul'Gurub, and when the Darkspear left the jungle with Thrall the boy was lost to them. Nimboya means to find him. He hunts the Bloodscalp tribe for answers, inspecting the shrunken heads of their victims in dread of finding Yenniku among them. If the Bloodscalps have killed the boy, he swears, a curse of six hundred years will fall on the spirit of their chief, Gan'zulah.

title: Zanzil the Outcast
body: Zanzil the Outcast is a troll witch doctor exiled by his own people, whose leaders fear his gift for bending the minds of others. He brews a mixture of jungle plants that strengthens the bodies of those who take it while suppressing their will, and his followers at the ruins of Aboraz and Jubuwal, trolls, naga and walking dead alike, are the result. Zanzil seized the Darkspear boy Yenniku and holds him body and soul, so that only the most potent magic could set him free. In Booty Bay there are buyers who would pay well for his mixture.

title: Captain Hecklebury Smotts
body: Captain Hecklebury Smotts once sailed a ship between Booty Bay and Ratchet and enjoyed a sterling reputation, until sea giants smashed his vessel, killed his crew and set him adrift in a lifeboat. One of them, Gorlash, carried off his captain's chest to keep as a snuffbox. Smotts bought another ship, named it Smotts' Revenge and went hunting the giants, only to lose it the same way, while the giant Negolash took his cutlass. By his own count three giants have ruined him three times, and the last of them, Mok'rash, still bellows his name across the water.
sources: quests 614/8551, 615/8553 descriptions

title: The Great Hunt
body: Hemet Nesingwary Jr. does not let just anyone join his expedition. A newcomer must first prove a steady hand against the beasts of the jungle under three masters. Ajeck Rouack, who learned tiger hunting from her father as a girl, starts her pupils on young cats near the camp and works up to the elder tigers. Sir S. J. Erlgadin does the same with panthers, and Hemet himself with raptors, from the common breeds to the cagey jungle stalkers. Each line ends with a beast no hunter has yet brought down: the tigress Sin'Dall, the elusive panther Bhag'thera and the treacherous raptor Tethis. Only one who has slain all three is offered the true prize, the great white tiger King Bangalash, the beast that drew Hemet to Stranglethorn in the first place.
sources: quests 583, 185-188, 190-193, 194-197, 208 (descriptions and reward texts)

title: The Green Hills of Stranglethorn
body: Hemet Nesingwary set down his adventures in the Vale as a novel, The Green Hills of Stranglethorn, and entrusted the manuscript to Barnil Stonepot to proofread. Then a gust of wind tore through the camp and scattered the pages across the jungle, and Barnil, dreading his master's reaction, quietly asks for help gathering them. The four chapters tell of the camp beside the old docks, of Ajeck's arrow felling a river crocolisk beside Barnil, of a tiger finished with a thrown axe, and of a panther crushed by a falling branch after a clumsy shot with a dwarven rifle. The tale ends with the hunters trapped on a sea cliff by lashtail raptors, saved only when a great white tiger charged in from the side and scattered the pack.
sources: page_text 124-181 (the novel)
notes: Crocolisk detail and the white tiger rescue aligned with page_text 130 and 180; rest verified.

title: Kurzen's Rebels
body: The rebels of Lieutenant Doren's camp fight a war they cannot win by numbers. Sergeant Yohwa answers with Kurzen's own covert tactics, sending raiders into the compound to cut down jungle fighters and seize the medicine men's remedies, then into the Stockpile against Kurzen's special forces. Meanwhile Private Thorsen, secretly sent to rejoin Kurzen's men as a spy, is nearly killed when his secret reaches the enemy, and Doren suspects a traitor. Bookie Herod's records, a hidden brass key and a strongbox in the Stockpile turn up a note signed only with an M, and the patrol rolls point to Private Merle. At last Doren sends champions into the cavern to face the colonel himself. Brother Nimetz, studying troll tablets and Skullsplitter fetishes, comes to believe the true villain is Mai'Zoth, and asks that he be slain as well.

title: The Fate of Yenniku
body: Nimboya's search for his chief's son begins in blood. Believing the Bloodscalps hold Yenniku, he sends hunters for their tusks and then for the shrunken heads of their headhunters, which he inspects one by one. Finding no sign of the boy, he turns to darker means: the heads of the Bloodscalp chief Gan'zulah and his witch doctor Nezzliok are placed in a cauldron and made to speak. Their spirits demand appeasement, trophy skulls stolen from the Skullsplitters and the shattered armor of Ana'thek the Cruel, before they reveal the truth: Yenniku is held by Zanzil the Outcast. Kin'weelay of Grom'gol, the mightiest Darkspear witch doctor, then seeks the Mind's Eye from Mai'Zoth, attunes it with singing shards from the Crystalvein Mine and reshapes it into a soul gem. Yenniku's soul is captured within it and carried back to Nimboya, and the Darkspear vow to remember the deed in song.

title: The Bloodsail Buccaneers
body: Rumors of Bloodsail pirates all over southern Stranglethorn send First Mate Crazz of the Blackwater Raiders looking for a scout. In a skiff hidden in a cove north of Booty Bay lies a map marked with an X on that very spot, with orders to wait for a signal from the southern command post before attacking. Fleet Master Seahorn has that post on the Wild Shore raided, and the captured charts and orders lay bare Firallon's plan: ships closing in, guns to seal the harbor, a landing party to burn the town and slay its leaders. Seahorn strikes first, sending a small band to kill Firallon and his captains Keelhaul and Stillwater. The Bloodsails recruit as well. Outsiders who make themselves enemies of Booty Bay are welcomed aboard the Crimson Veil and sent to put a knife in Seahorn and Revilgaz.

title: The Stone of the Tides
body: Sailors in the Booty Bay tavern whisper of a haunted island off the coast, home to water elementals and a raving goblin ghost. Baron Revilgaz knows the legend behind the tale. The Stone of the Tides, a blue stone shot through with milky strands, once gave Gurubashi warriors command over water, and each bearer, honored as Tidebearer, slowly faded from existence until he walked into the sea. Revilgaz suspects the goblin wizard Gazban found it. Bracers from Gazban's elementals go to Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver of the Kirin Tor, who knows of a troll dagger able to overpower the stone's altar, but he gave it to his daughter Catelyn, who ran off to become a pirate and then lost it to 'Pretty Boy' Duncan of the Bloodsail. With the blade recovered, the altar in the sunken troll city is overcome, and the Stone takes pride of place in the baron's collection.
